motivation: arbbot is a personal Polymarket/Kalshi prediction-market arbitrage bot: a Rust trading engine under rust/ (recorder, book builder, scanner, quoter, ledger) and a Python layer under src/arbbot, scripts/, and tests/ for recording, registry compilation, reporting, and research tooling.

The Rust workspace enforces a zero-warning clippy and lint policy recorded in rust/Cargo.toml, and the money-path logic (fills, ledger, maker-exit, risk) is covered by unit and integration tests that read like specifications of what must never happen.
The project is pre-live: Stage 1 is record-and-scan only, so changes should preserve measurement correctness (book state, fee accounting, registry parsing) rather than add trading capability.
acceptanceCriteria: cargo test --workspace passes for any change touching rust/, excluding the one test that requires the private, gitignored config/registry.yaml.
pytest (run from the project's .venv) passes for any change touching src/, scripts/, or tests/.
No change adds files under data/, credentials/, or the private registry/topics files listed in .gitignore.
constraints: The repository's default branch is main.
config/registry.yaml, config/registry-rejected.yaml, and config/topics.yaml are intentionally untracked; do not add them or hardcode their contents elsewhere.
Keep changes scoped to what the task asks: match existing style in rust/ and src/arbbot, and do not reorganize, reformat, or refactor code the task does not touch.

instructions: Read the specific crate, module, or script you are changing, and its existing tests, before editing it.
For Rust changes, keep cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace clean against the lint policy in rust/Cargo.toml, and add or update unit/integration tests alongside behavior changes.
For Python changes, add or update tests under tests/ alongside behavior changes, and keep the venv-based workflow (uv venv && uv pip install -e '.[dev]') working.
Do not touch config/registry.yaml, config/registry-rejected.yaml, config/topics.yaml, or anything under data/ or credentials/ - these are private and intentionally outside version control.
Keep the change minimal and scoped to the task; do not refactor or reformat unrelated code.
Confirm the diff is scoped to the task, with no unrelated refactors, formatting, or dead-code removal.
For Rust changes, confirm the workspace lint policy in rust/Cargo.toml still holds and that money-path invariants (fee accounting, ledger balance, maker-exit gauges) are not weakened.
For Python changes, confirm new or changed behavior has matching test coverage under tests/.
Confirm no secrets, credentials, or files under data/ or the private registry/topics config files were added.
